data.description:
## Context

The six calibration program epics (a03c-d55e, 94ed-f55c, d566-afa6, 7f42-e41f, 69e8-af39, 411b-a047) collectively produce rich per-event measurement signals — reviewer findings per PR, intent-coverage findings per closure, mutation kill rates per PR, negative-example extractions per /dso:fix-bug invocation, graduation telemetry per /dso:retro. None of them aggregate over time. The headline program metric — 'what fraction of bugs are caught by tests vs other channels (review, production), and is the ratio improving?' — is uncomputable today because per-event data lives in disjoint stores (ticket comments, GHA artifacts, reviewer-findings.json on the tickets branch) without a rollup layer.

This epic delivers the program-level observability surface: bug-detection-channel attribution (the missing primitive), time-aggregated rollup tooling, trend tracking, and program health reporting. Tickets-as-storage pattern throughout — rollups accumulate as comments on dedicated tracking tickets so they remain searchable.

## Scope (refine via brainstorm)

In:
- detected_by classification field on bug tickets (rolled in from cf65-e3b4 — now closed). Allowed values: tests, review-llm, review-human, production, user-report, internal-dogfood, other. Tag pattern detected_by:<channel>. /dso:create-bug and /dso:fix-bug elicit the field. 411b auto-bugs set detected_by:tests. 69e8 graduation uses detected_by as candidate weighting.
- Time-aggregated rollup skill or script (/dso:test-quality-report or equivalent) that queries the ticket system, persisted reviewer-findings, 411b mutation findings, and 69e8 retro telemetry to produce per-month / per-quarter rollups
- Headline program metrics surfaced: bug-detection-channel breakdown over time; Tier 1/Tier 2 reviewer finding rates; per-stack mutation kill-rate trends; suite size and growth rate; intent-coverage breadth; standard-rule effectiveness (bugs of type X before vs after rule graduation)
- Per-PR suite-churn telemetry: test count delta (added, removed, modified) tracked over time on a dedicated suite-churn-history ticket
- Cross-epic query helper for joining manifest + headers + mutation findings + bug data (e.g., 'show me intent items with low mutation kill rate')
- Long-term mutation-finding archival: extend retention beyond GHA's default 90-day window by appending per-PR kill-rate summary stats as comments on a dedicated mutation-history-<year-month> tracking ticket
- Tickets-as-storage: rollups are comments on tracking tickets; queryable via ticket CLI

Out:
- Test-caught-regression event tagging from CI logs — deferred (P3+ follow-on)
- Custom dashboards / web UI — out of scope; surface is ticket comments + script output
- Real-time streaming metrics — periodic rollups only

## Dependencies

Soft consumers (epic consumes their outputs; no hard blocking):
- a03c-d55e — closure-checks-aware verifier findings
- 94ed-f55c — intent allocation manifest
- d566-afa6 — Tier 1/Tier 2 reviewer findings
- 7f42-e41f — intent-coverage findings (orphan_intent rate, header_source_mismatch rate)
- 69e8-af39 — retro graduation telemetry, negative-example extraction rate
- 411b-a047 — per-PR mutation kill rates, threshold-breach auto-bugs
- 4911-c7ba — bug-type-<slug> taxonomy (joined with detected_by for cross-classification reporting)

This epic ships AFTER (or alongside) the calibration program epics produce data to aggregate. detected_by attribution work blocks the rest of the rollup work — without it, the headline metric is uncomputable.

## Why this exists

Per the gap analysis surfaced at session-end: the calibration program ships substantial per-event measurement infrastructure but no aggregation layer. Without this epic, the program's success/failure cannot be measured at the headline level. The maintainer would have rich per-PR data but no way to see 'is the test-writing system improving over time?'

Refine via /dso:brainstorm.
data.title: Calibration program observability: rollup metrics, trend tracking, bug-detection-channel attribution, and program-level health reporting
